title: Teluni Human Identity and Access Policies
heading: Status and ownership
text:
Status and ownership
**Decided product policies, 2026-10-18:** the owner answered all 38 PH-11 questions directly. This document owns human enrollment, authentication assurance, recovery, sessions, permission allocation and support policy. The inherited [authentication](../security/authentication.md) and [authorization](../security/authorization.md) controls still govern. [Release policies](release-policies.md) own publication/playback behavior; this policy constrains who can trigger it.
**Accepted provider direction:** self-hosted Keycloak, with the [pinned-source compatibility assessment](identity-provider-evaluation.md#pinned-source-assessment) and owner acceptance recorded on 2026-10-18. Actual deployment remains subject to PH-10 host feasibility and PJ-24 integration qualification. No recurring identity/email procurement budget is authorized. This does not establish zero operating cost or an available email service. Google is the only selected external login provider; Microsoft is not part of this delivery.
**Accepted architecture:** the owner explicitly approved [ADR-0024](../adr/0024-propose-keycloak-and-server-managed-human-sessions.md) and [ADR-0025](../adr/0025-propose-application-owned-scoped-access-profiles.md) on 2026-10-18. They do not supersede accepted ADR-0012. **Implemented:** foundation JWT verification only; no product login, provider deployment, session/membership store or permission engine exists. PH-11 is completed for provider/policy/architecture selection; every unperformed integration test remains PJ-03/PJ-24. This documentation does not authorize implementation or external provisioning.

title: Teluni Human Identity and Access Policies
heading: Enrollment and account continuity
text:
Enrollment and account continuity
Support **public registration with automatic company activation** after verification and abuse checks, rather than requiring routine Teluni approval. The new company is separate from every existing company; matching a name, claimed business identifier or email domain never proves control of an existing tenant. Activation does not imply a free plan, trial duration, paid entitlement or unlimited resources. PH-12 must establish eligibility/entitlement/resource rules, and PH-13 the applicable notices, before public activation is opened. A pending prerequisite must not silently turn the selected product into invitation-only onboarding.
Offer email/password and optional passkeys through the established identity provider, plus optional Google login. Do not make an external social account the sole administrative recovery method. Localized enrollment/login/recovery must support `pt-BR` and `en-US`.
Require trusted email verification before company access. Company invitations are recipient-bound, single-use, revocable and valid for **seven days**; a resend invalidates the previous pending invitation. Acceptance requires the matching authenticated identity and explicit membership confirmation. Changing recipient requires a new invitation. Verification establishes mailbox control, not legal identity or company ownership.
Link login methods only through an explicit flow proving the existing account and new method with recent authentication. Never merge accounts solely by equal email. A new email must be verified, the previous address notified and the stable application identity preserved. Method removal must leave a usable method meeting assurance requirements. This applies equally to first Google login and later linking.
One human identity may hold independent memberships in multiple companies and different scopes/roles within each. Switching company explicitly revalidates access. A company administrator cannot enumerate the person's other companies or manage their global credentials.
Each company has a **designated responsible administrator** who approves additional company administrators. Other administrators retain the matrix's ordinary administrative capabilities but cannot bypass that approval. Establish the first responsible administrator from the verified automatic signup flow; controlled assisted enrollment may serve support/migration needs without overriding the public-registration decision. Responsibility transfer requires an attributable, strongly authenticated flow and successor acceptance; prevent loss of the last active administrator or responsibility without a valid transfer. Responsibility is a company relationship, not an inferred legal-ownership determination or platform privilege.
Provision platform administrators through a controlled procedure, outside public signup and tenant administration. Use individual administrative accounts distinct from ordinary customer operation, with phishing-resistant assurance and prepared recovery. Product administration does not grant access to provider administration, infrastructure, database credentials or customer content.

title: Teluni Human Identity and Access Policies
heading: Assurance, recovery and abuse
text:
Assurance, recovery and abuse
Strong authentication is mandatory for platform administrators, company administrators and branch managers. Operators may opt in, and companies can require it for everyone. Any operator/profile granted publication or automatic-price distribution must also meet the strong-authentication requirement. Do not let custom role labels bypass an assurance requirement attached to a capability.
Prefer passkeys with user verification; password plus an authenticator-app second factor is the selected alternative, with protected single-use recovery codes. Platform administration requires a phishing-resistant method and protected recovery. Social login or a generic passkey label does not alone prove equivalent assurance: qualify the actual flow and assertion. Email-only recovery cannot bypass mandatory MFA. Do not use SMS as the default method.
Require strong authentication no more than **five minutes** old when promoting administrators, changing credentials/MFA/email, transferring responsibility, granting support access, exporting in bulk or unlinking/destroying in bulk. Ordinary authorized publication/price operations use the normal compliant session, without a new prompt for every save. Sensitive operations by users without an enrolled adequate factor must first obtain the required assurance. Confirmation dialogs do not constitute authentication.
Use provider-owned password recovery with enumeration-safe public responses. The selected reset-link target is **15 minutes**, single-purpose and single-use; verify exact invalidation semantics in the selected version. Successful password recovery revokes earlier sessions. MFA recovery first uses a valid alternate authenticator or recovery code. Suspected compromise offers global session termination and a support channel.
Complete loss of recovery methods uses exceptional assisted recovery with proportionate evidence, waiting/notification to previous channels, review and audit. The operational procedure, waiting interval, evidence criteria and escalation remain to be reviewed before use; no instant-unlock promise is made. Seek independent review for higher-risk cases when available, without claiming a two-person control in a one-person operation. Insufficient evidence denies access. Do not introduce personal security questions, agent-created temporary passwords or email-only removal of MFA. Company administrators may repair local membership but cannot reset another person's global identity. Prepare a separate accountable recovery path for the sole platform administrator/last responsible company administrator.
Apply context/operation rate limits, progressive delays, enumeration-safe responses and monitoring, without permanent attacker-triggered lockout. Additional challenges need demonstrated need, accessibility/privacy review and cost approval; they are not a default on every interaction. Numerical anti-abuse limits and provider password-policy parameters require technical review rather than invented vendor defaults. No external challenge subscription is authorized.

List sessions using minimized, justified metadata; allow termination of one or all. Background polling/refresh does not count as human activity and cannot extend absolute duration. Warn before timeout and protect recoverable drafts without leaking them across account/company changes or retaining protected caches after logout. Detailed concurrent-session accounting across provider and application sessions remains design/qualification work.
**Accepted browser architecture, not implemented:** server-managed application sessions with an opaque protected browser cookie; provider access/refresh tokens remain server-side. Compose this capability into the modular backend where appropriate rather than adding a microservice by default. Use established OIDC Authorization Code with PKCE and established session/security components; do not invent token issuance, crypto or password handling. Evaluate `Secure`, `HttpOnly`, `SameSite`, narrow cookie scope, explicit CSRF protection, state/nonce/redirect validation, fixation prevention, refresh rotation/replay/concurrency, logout propagation and token minimization. No cookie names, routes, storage library or environment variables are implemented by this policy.
The internal API bearer boundary remains ADR-0012. A browser cookie must terminate at a reviewed session boundary that obtains the legitimate issuer access token; it is not a second implicit credential accepted by every domain route. The current verifier returns principal ID/scopes, not session or assurance evidence; extend integration contracts deliberately through technical review rather than trusting browser-supplied session IDs, role flags, timestamps or MFA claims.
Validate current application account/session/membership state in addition to JWT signature/expiry to meet the 30-second bound. Cache invalidation, session linkage and sensitive-write race handling need explicit implementation evidence. A valid five-minute JWT alone cannot satisfy that bound. Provider logout and application logout must be reconciled, including reuse/replay and local/global termination. Human logout does not revoke unrelated company memberships or player identities.
On provider, email or session infrastructure failure, unavailable flows report a safe temporary failure. Existing operations continue only while trusted identity, validity and authorization can still be established; otherwise deny protected operations and preserve recoverable work safely. A key/session-store outage is not permission to skip checks. There is no offline administrative panel or public emergency credential. Players retain their independently selected bounded offline policy, not these human-session limits.

Permission model and default matrix
Support readable default roles plus company-customized profiles built from explicit business capabilities and scopes. The application owns memberships, profiles and resource authorization, not arbitrary provider groups or self-editable identity attributes. Check company, branch, resource, operation, assurance and current state on the server, including background jobs and generated data. This is a product policy; the accepted technical direction is ADR-0025; its concrete mechanism and verification remain implementation work.
Grants combine within their explicit scopes. A person can manage one branch and observe another. A suspended account/membership or expired grant always denies; no grant means deny. Newly created branches do not silently enter a restricted branch grant. Company-wide administrative scope is an explicit grant. Avoid arbitrary negative-rule languages, cyclic inheritance or an unrestricted role shortcut. Grantors cannot confer authority they lack; company grants never confer platform authority. Profile edits must show affected users/scopes and be audited.

title: Teluni Human Identity and Access Policies
heading: Publication impact and delayed work
text:
Publication impact and delayed work
An authorized designated price save triggers automatic publication under PH-09. Before accepting it, authorize the mutation **and all affected published targets**. If any target is outside scope, **reject the entire price mutation** with a safe explanation. Do not partially distribute it, modify the company base price anyway or create an out-of-scope approval request as an automatic fallback. An explicit authorized branch override may be used only when the model and local impact permit it. A permitted shared edit cannot grant hidden publication power.
Authorized publishers normally publish directly. A company may optionally require independent approval by branch/operation; default is disabled, with no self-approval where required. For covered prices, entering a proposal is not saving an effective price: the authorized approval commits that price and triggers automatic publication. This explicit policy qualifies the PH-09 save behavior without turning ordinary drafts into live content. P27 still requires denying an out-of-scope price mutation; optional approvals do not provide a bypass. Approval-chain configuration must identify eligible reviewers, prevent scope escalation and clearly distinguish proposed, approved, saved, queued and active states. No approval module is implemented or inherited from Orion's removed reference feature.
Revalidate company/actor/target authority before an outstanding intent effects a protected change/publication. If authority has been removed/reduced, block the not-yet-effected intent and require new attributable authorization, retaining original authorship. A valid version already authorized and issued continues its normal delivery lifecycle; removing its author does not automatically cancel company programming. Incident response may revoke specific publications/identities. Revalidation cannot silently expand old targets or allow stale work to overwrite newer generations.
Company administrators remove only the local membership; other memberships and global identity remain. Departure does not delete company content. Global disablement is an identity operation. Company suspension denies new protected server operations, with explicit reconciliation for already-authorized offline players; PH-12 owns commercial/cancellation consequences. Historical attribution remains meaningful subject to PH-13 retention/deletion rules. Never promise instantaneous erasure of unreachable devices.

title: Teluni Human Identity and Access Policies
heading: Support, audit and continuity
text:
Support, audit and continuity
Routine customer-content support requires an explicit company-administrator grant: reason, scope, maximum default duration **one hour**, read-only default and separate write authority. Support uses its own identity, with visible/audited activity; **no impersonation in this delivery**. Platform operations may manage customer lifecycle metadata without implicit content browsing. A support grant never authorizes provider/database/infrastructure access.
Emergency access requires a distinct exceptional procedure with justification, strong authentication, scope, expiry, audit and notification afterward where applicable. It creates no permanent secret user, universal password or unrestricted standing customer-content access. Evidence criteria, available reviewers and execution/revocation steps must be reviewed before use, honestly reflecting team size. A routine support grant is not emergency authority.
Users can review their sessions and receive relevant credential/recovery notices. Company administrators see company-scoped audit; branch managers see only their branch operations. The platform receives minimized events needed for security/operation. Audit invites, grants/profile changes, assurance/recovery/revocation, support, prices/publications and relevant failures with actor/scope/action/outcome, excluding secrets and full payloads. Security-audit retention and metadata such as IP remain PH-13; the PH-09 operational-report retention is not a legal/security retention decision.
Require application-stable principal IDs, application-owned memberships/permissions, isolated environments and synthetic test identities. Back up/restore identity state under PH-10 and reconcile revocations after restoration. Portability is required, but P37=A does **not** require a pre-pilot export/import proof as a separate acceptance gate; qualify migration when selected/needed and document available mechanisms/limits. A migration may require safe password reset or authenticator reenrollment; do not promise export of every factor or session. No production credentials in CI or cross-environment token acceptance.

title: Teluni Human Identity and Access Policies
heading: Required verification cases
text:
Required verification cases
These are specified allow/deny and lifecycle cases, **not executed tests**. PJ-03/PJ-24 own implementation evidence; PJ-07 owns design review.
Case
Required expected result
IA-01 — Public enrollment
Verified eligible signup creates a new isolated company and its responsible administrator; cannot claim an existing tenant, set privileged principal claims or gain platform authority
IA-02 — Invitation and linking
Correct verified recipient accepts once within seven days; wrong recipient, replay, revoked/replaced/expired invite and email-only account merging fail
IA-03 — Company context
One identity uses independently scoped memberships; switching/reusing IDs, mixed-tenant references, collections, counts, downloads and caches cannot cross scope
IA-04 — Responsibility
Responsible administrator approves additional administrators; ordinary admin cannot bypass it; last-admin removal and incomplete transfer fail
IA-05 — Assurance
Required roles/capabilities cannot bypass MFA; sensitive actions require trusted assurance no older than five minutes; social/weak recovery cannot satisfy it implicitly
IA-06 — Recovery
Reset-link expiry/single use, MFA recovery and earlier-session revocation work; insufficient assisted-recovery evidence cannot grant access or affect unrelated memberships
IA-07 — Sessions
Idle/absolute limits, no remember-me, five-session/two-platform-context bounds and explicit termination work across tabs, refresh concurrency and logout
IA-08 — Revocation
Global/session/local removal and profile reductions prevent new operations within 30 seconds; stale JWT/grants cannot authorize sensitive effects; unrelated memberships remain available
IA-09 — Browser boundary
OIDC state/nonce/PKCE/redirect checks, protected cookies, CSRF/fixation controls, token redaction and server-only token storage resist bypass; provider logout/refresh replay are reconciled
IA-10 — Scoped profiles
Matrix allow cases work; operator publish/delete/export, manager cross-branch actions, unauthorized grants/profile edits and temporary-grant expiry fail closed
IA-11 — Price impact
Authorized all-target save publishes; any unauthorized target rejects the whole mutation without a partial save/distribution or hidden approval fallback; authorized local override stays local
IA-12 — Optional approvals
Disabled policy allows authorized direct publication; enabled policy requires independent scoped approval and never labels a price proposal already effective
IA-13 — Delayed work
Removal/reduction blocks an outstanding protected effect; issued valid publications continue normally; retries do not expand scope or lose real authorship
IA-14 — Support/emergency
No default customer-content privilege; scoped consent expires within its grant, read grants cannot write, no impersonation, exceptional access follows separately reviewed controls
IA-15 — Failure and continuity
Identity/JWKS/session/email outages fail safely without administrative bypass; environments, restore and migration preserve principal scope/revocation and independent player behavior
IA-16 — Evidence and abuse
Safe public errors, bounded abuse controls, audit access/notifications and redaction preserve attribution without enumerating identities or leaking secrets

title: Teluni Identity Provider Evaluation
heading: Evaluation scope and result
text:
Evaluation scope and result
On **2026-10-18**, the owner selected self-hosting and **Keycloak**, then explicitly approved all pending Teluni ADRs, including ADR-0024/ADR-0025. Host feasibility and actual integration qualification remain delivery prerequisites. No recurring identity/email procurement budget is available. This is a documentation/source review, not a deployed-provider experiment, security assessment or proof of operational capacity. Keycloak **26.8.1**, release published on 2026-10-13, was inspected at source commit `24ed1dadf3f246a555adb6d3d4a99e9b3003fb3b` for the assessment below. This pins review evidence only; no deployment image/digest has been selected or installed. Reassess the deployment version and security status before implementation; mutable `latest` documentation does not pin a production dependency.
The existing [verifier](../../apps/api/src/authentication.ts) and accepted [ADR-0012](../adr/0012-verify-jwt-access-tokens-at-the-first-api-boundary.md) are the executable/governing boundary. Do not weaken it because a candidate emits different defaults. The source/documentation review and explicit owner approval satisfy PH-11's architectural decision scope. They do not qualify a running integration. Required policies and measured bounds remain in the [identity policy](identity-and-access.md), not vendor defaults.

Pinned-source evidence / accepted integration responsibility
Exact `typ=at+jwt`
[DefaultTokenManager](https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/blob/24ed1dadf3f246a555adb6d3d4a99e9b3003fb3b/services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/jose/jws/DefaultTokenManager.java) selects the RFC 9068 access-token header when the client option is enabled; [OIDCConfigAttributes](https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/blob/24ed1dadf3f246a555adb6d3d4a99e9b3003fb3b/server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/OIDCConfigAttributes.java) defines `access.token.header.type.rfc9068`. Configure it explicitly; do not change the existing verifier's accepted type
Signed tokens and exact issuer/audience
The signing path in DefaultTokenManager uses the configured signature provider. [TokenManager](https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/blob/24ed1dadf3f246a555adb6d3d4a99e9b3003fb3b/services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/TokenManager.java) sets issuer; [SubMapper](https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/blob/24ed1dadf3f246a555adb6d3d4a99e9b3003fb3b/services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/mappers/SubMapper.java) supplies the persistent user subject; [AudienceProtocolMapper](https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/blob/24ed1dadf3f246a555adb6d3d4a99e9b3003fb3b/services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/mappers/AudienceProtocolMapper.java) adds the configured audience. The integration must select RS256 or ES256 and the exact trusted API issuer/audience/JWKS, then test actual signatures/key rotation and denial cases
`sub`, `iat`, `exp`, string `scope`
TokenManager initializes access tokens from the authenticated user/session and sets the scope string; [AccessToken](https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/blob/24ed1dadf3f246a555adb6d3d4a99e9b3003fb3b/core/src/main/java/org/keycloak/representations/AccessToken.java) and [JsonWebToken](https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/blob/24ed1dadf3f246a555adb6d3d4a99e9b3003fb3b/core/src/main/java/org/keycloak/representations/JsonWebToken.java) define their representation/time lifecycle. Actual emitted types, clock bounds and expiry remain verifier integration tests
Application principal UUID
[UserAttributeMapper](https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/blob/24ed1dadf3f246a555adb6d3d4a99e9b3003fb3b/services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/mappers/UserAttributeMapper.java) maps a configured user attribute into a configured token claim. Trusted provisioning must generate an application UUID, keep a unique stable `(issuer, subject)` association and map a non-user-editable attribute to `orion_principal_id`. User profile edits, signup, Google imports and tenant administrators cannot create/replace that attribute; fail closed until the trusted mapping exists
Trusted human assertion
[HardcodedClaim](https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/blob/24ed1dadf3f246a555adb6d3d4a99e9b3003fb3b/services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/mappers/HardcodedClaim.java) can supply `orion_actor_type=human` only in a restricted human-login client/flow. Disable service-account, password/direct-grant and unreviewed exchange/impersonation paths on that client; a constant mapper alone does not prove a human. Test that machine credentials cannot produce an accepted human token
Session/assurance freshness
The current verifier deliberately returns only principal/scopes. The reviewed OIDC boundary must bind verified login assertions and current server session/assurance state to that principal and the legitimate access token. An ID token may establish login context at its intended OIDC boundary but never substitutes for the API access token. Enforce the 30-second session/membership revocation goal using application state, not unimplemented claims or provider logout alone
The review found a viable standards-based mapping path without changing ADR-0012. It does not assert that a default Keycloak client/token already meets the contract. Immutable principal provisioning, protected profile attributes, human-only flow restrictions and trusted session/assurance binding are mandatory implementation design/control requirements under PJ-07/PJ-24, not controls that were deployed in this task. Deployment version/image selection remains PH-15/PJ-24.

Direction

title: Teluni Implementation Plan
heading: Maintaining this plan
text:
Maintaining this plan
Every contributor or coding agent performing implementation work must maintain this plan and the [project human actions](human-actions.md) within the user's authorized scope.
Before implementation, inspect actual repository state, the relevant task, its prerequisites, governing policy, and linked human actions. Do not treat a planned capability or unchecked action as available.
Mark a task `in progress` when work actually starts. Update statuses when evidence, scope, dependencies, or blockers change, and before each handoff or completion report.
Allocate stable task IDs as `PJ-NN`; never reuse or renumber them. Add finer tasks when needed; do not hide unfinished subtasks inside a completed row.
Record concise evidence in the task row: implementation paths, validation commands and results, review references, or a linked decision. Record evidence produced for this repository—local validation, this repository's CI runs, and this repository's external settings. Do not store secret values or sensitive output.
A task becomes `completed` only when its deliverables and acceptance criteria are satisfied with evidence. A partial implementation or an unavailable required check is not completion.
When human intervention is necessary, add or update a project human action, link it from the affected task, mark that task `blocked`, and tell the user what is needed. Continue independent authorized work where possible.
A future prerequisite is `pending`, not automatically `blocked`.
When scope or sequencing changes, use `changed`, explain why and what replaces the work, and link supporting decisions. Do not delete unresolved obligations to make the plan look complete.
Update command availability, current documentation, generated artifacts, and the human actions in the same coherent change where applicable. Do not change ADR status merely to record implementation progress.
Status
Meaning
`pending`
Not started; includes conditional work whose trigger has not occurred.
`in progress`
Work has started and is incomplete.
`completed`
Applicable deliverables and acceptance criteria are satisfied with evidence.
`blocked`
The identified work cannot proceed without a recorded dependency, decision, access, or correction.
`changed`
Scope, applicability, or sequencing was explicitly revised; reason and replacement or disposition are recorded.

**Decided:** complete the company-to-screen journey with tenant-safe remote management, images/videos, configurable data catalogs, freeform simultaneous content, regional schedules, offline Android TV playback and monitoring. The owner prioritizes intended product capability/quality over reducing scope solely to fit an MVP label. The historical `mvp.md` path remains the stable requirements entry point.

The [plan](implementation-plan.md) owns delivery status; [release policies](release-policies.md) own business behavior and the questionnaire decision record; [acceptance targets](release-targets.md) own numeric limits and qualification goals. Functional requirement
Required acceptance evidence before release

Companies, branches, users, company settings, public company signup/automatic activation, authentication, scoped standard/custom profiles and temporary access
Two synthetic companies each have branches/users. Authorized members manage allowed resources; direct API attempts, lists/search, media/catalog access and identifier substitution cannot cross company/branch scope. Verify responsible-administrator approval, trusted account linking, strong/recent authentication, recovery, session bounds and 30-second revocation using [IA-01–IA-16](identity-and-access.md#required-verification-cases). Public activation must satisfy commercial/privacy/abuse gates; platform operation has no implicit customer-content access.
FR-02
Device identity, temporary-code pairing, company/branch assignment, name/configuration and safe unlink
An authorized user claims a displayed code once. Expired/replayed codes, concurrent claims, wrong-scope assignment and revoked identities fail safely. Reassignment requires verified cleanup/reset and cannot expose previous tenant data/credentials; unreachable erasure is shown as pending.
FR-03
Supported horizontal/vertical orientation
Qualified devices display supported orientations correctly; invalid geometry or unsupported profiles have explicit outcomes rather than silent support claims.
FR-04
Private image/video upload, validation, organization, metadata, reuse, conversion and reference-aware deletion
Approved profiles upload, validate/convert and play on tested hardware. Spoofed type, malformed/oversized content and unauthorized reads fail safely. Archive/deletion/retention preserve protected draft, active, staging and recovery references; assisted draft changes need confirmation.
FR-05
Playlists, ordered items, configurable image duration, full-video playback, looping, device/group assignment and qualified cuts/fades
Deterministic order and preview/player duration agreement. Devices have zero or one company-owned group, including cross-branch groups; explicit individual programming replaces the whole group source. Confirmed source changes use published content or an intentionally empty destination. Ordinary item completion and coordinated-page timing follow release policies.
FR-06
Dates, local hours, weekdays, overnight recurrence, regional schedules and deterministic conflict/no-match rules
Shared backend/player fixtures cover inclusive starts/exclusive ends, final-date clipping, all-day/equal-time validation, timezone/DST, overlapping same-output windows, regional exceptions and empty windows. Optional defaults otherwise give safe neutral output; expired commercial content is not an implicit fallback.
FR-07
Preview, publication, immutable consistent versions, desired/downloaded/active state and last-valid preservation
Ordinary drafts do not affect screens. Authorized price saves automatically publish affected published bindings through durable/retry-safe intent, excluding unrelated drafts. Concurrent/repeated operations and unknown outcomes are reconcilable. Complete supported versions activate only after validated staging; failures never replace valid state with mixed/corrupt resources.
FR-08
Android TV playback, bounded offline operation and controlled recovery/update
Qualified devices play local media/catalog snapshots without normal backend streaming, through the selected offline/clock/authorization envelope, reboot, power interruption and protocol/update cases in playback acceptance. Expired authorization or untrusted time has an explicit safe outcome.
FR-09
Scoped connection/last-contact/app/storage/sync/playback diagnostics
Show observed timestamps, stale/offline thresholds and actual version states. Distinguish failed sync, regional rendering failure and lost contact from stopped playback. Reconnection reconciles state without leaking data or claiming unseen erasure.
FR-10
Freeform simultaneous composition, independent areas with optional coordinated pages, per-area schedules, multiple videos and configurable mixed audio
Users position/resize areas and preview copy/import/export of versioned textual layouts. An active regional schedule survives a global page change; coordinated areas follow the selected page timeline. Isolated area failure/no-match preserves unaffected geometry/output. Qualified rendering/audio profiles and pagination remain readable and work offline.
FR-11
User-defined typed catalogs, fields and records with layout bindings, including products/prices and weekly agendas
Users configure a non-product catalog as well as a product configuration. Validate schema/version evolution, scoped record/media references, branch price overrides and import boundaries. Data-driven views paginate without silent name/price clipping. Price publication/expiry and unavailable-item defaults work from consistent offline snapshots; customization cannot execute arbitrary code or cross tenant boundaries.
Managed campaigns remain future scope; scheduled content and published price-validity rules provide the initial promotion behavior without approving a separate campaign engine.

title: Teluni Initial Release Requirements and Acceptance
heading: Release acceptance journey
text:
Release acceptance journey
Establish two synthetic companies through verified enrollment with responsible administrators, differently scoped branches/operators and qualified Android TV devices. Exercise IA-01–IA-16 login/linking/recovery/session/revocation/approval/support cases and API/media/catalog allow/deny boundaries; no implicit platform content privilege.
Pair devices, create a cross-branch group and an explicit individual exception. Upload media; configure a custom weekly-agenda catalog and product/price configuration. Compose independent and coordinated areas, regional schedules and an optional default; preview and publish A.
Verify local multi-video/audio/catalog rendering under the qualified profile. Edit drafts without changing A. Save a price and verify automatic consistent publication from published dependencies without leaking unrelated drafts; test concurrent edits, duplicate delivery and failed/unknown outcomes.
Publish B while playback continues. Cut network/power at download/staging/activation boundaries and verify complete valid A or B. Isolate a runtime regional fault without confusing it with incomplete-generation activation. Check protected references and insufficient disk outcomes.
Exercise schedule/date/DST/promotion/no-match/pagination and regional-page timing offline. Test the trusted-clock and authorization deadlines, restart/recovery and the expected safe neutral states.
Reconnect and reconcile observed state. Unlink/revoke while offline, then verify cleanup before cross-company pairing. Exercise historical recovery without expired offers or resurrected credentials and validate controlled protocol/app updates.
Rehearse database-plus-media restore and endpoint migration in isolation. Record target-linked load/usability/hardware evidence, costs and residual risk before real-customer acceptance.
Evidence includes automated contract/security/integration/browser tests, representative hardware/power/network tests, restore results and user observation. Delivery can be incremental; an operational release requires the complete applicable acceptance set. Passing foundation validation only checks currently implemented foundation/docs.

Explicitly outside the MVP
The historical heading remains a stable route; initial scope now includes freeform composition, configurable catalogs and their approved commercial defaults. Further unreviewed widgets, managed campaigns, external ERP/POS/partner integration APIs/webhooks/imports, automated billing/subscriptions, white-label, AI, playback analytics, general remote-control tools, impersonation, synchronization across separate screens and alternative players remain future unless independently approved. Generic fields do not approve arbitrary executable plugins, unrestricted data collection or all roadmap capabilities.

title: Teluni Deployment and Migration Planning
heading: Constraints and current state
text:
Constraints and current state
**Decided constraint:** no present cloud-service budget. The owner intends to use a personal residential server for development, tests and potentially initial customers, moving to a VPS/cloud when revenue or operational need justifies it. **Accepted initial architecture under ADR-0021:** Debian Linux, Docker Compose, a reverse proxy with HTTPS, local persistent media, automated backups and suitable monitoring. Real-customer use remains subject to PH-10 readiness gates. None is a deployed Teluni environment or executable procedure in this repository.
Follow inherited [production access](../security/production-access.md), [secrets management](../security/secrets-management.md), [retention](../security/data-retention.md), [observability](../reliability/observability.md), [alerting](../reliability/alerting.md), and [runbook authoring](../runbooks/authoring.md). This plan does not grant production authority. Write tested deployment/recovery runbooks when the environment exists, rather than speculative commands now.

title: Teluni Deployment and Migration Planning
heading: Residential exposure and readiness gate
text:
Residential exposure and readiness gate
[PH-10](human-actions.md#ph-10) requires an actual host/network inventory: CPU/RAM/disk and growth, upload bandwidth, data caps, power/reboot recovery, router/firewall, public address or CGNAT, ISP restrictions, available domain, certificate renewal, secure remote administration and backup connectivity. Keep private addresses, credentials and sensitive topology out of tracked public documentation.
A tunnel, free DNS option or any video-delivery intermediary requires evaluation of current terms, limits, privacy, security, transfer cost and failure behavior before selection. Do not assume Cloudflare Tunnel, DNS, or video distribution automatically provides an acceptable production path. No such provider is selected here.
Before any real pilot, record and demonstrate:
HTTPS works end to end; only intentional public application endpoints are exposed. PostgreSQL, orchestration dashboards and administrative interfaces remain private/restricted. Remote administration does not imply an unrestricted remote-control product feature.
Development/test and customer data, identities, credentials and backups are separated; logs/diagnostics are redacted; real data does not enter development fixtures.
Durable database and media survive container recreation, controlled app updates and host reboot. Schema migrations use reviewed release procedures and an explicit recovery plan.
Offline playback has been tested independently from backend availability. A home outage still prevents new uploads, publication, pairing, current monitoring and some recovery; communicate these limits to pilot participants.
The owner agrees measurable availability, maintenance, incident contact, backup RPO/RTO and support expectations. No commercial SLA is implied by the architecture.
Until verified, external exposure and real-customer operation are **pending**, even if development works locally.

title: Teluni Deployment and Migration Planning
heading: Persistent state and storage portability
text:
Persistent state and storage portability
Keep environment-specific URLs, credentials and paths in validated environment configuration; use only implemented keys from the [configuration reference](../generated/configuration/api.md) today. Define and document new keys with their future canonical schemas when implemented. Do not embed the residential hostname/path in business entities, contracts or player binaries.
**Accepted storage boundary:** the media capability owns object identity, integrity, metadata, authorized reads and lifecycle. Isolate the actual filesystem I/O behind a cohesive media-owned storage responsibility so a future S3-compatible implementation can preserve object semantics without rewriting domain rules. Avoid a general provider framework or mandatory S3 dependency now. Object-store replacement still needs verified access, integrity, migration and concurrency semantics; portability is not a free automatic migration.
Use durable logical object identifiers rather than storing temporary download credentials as business identity. External media endpoints are configurable. Authorized delivery may use an API or another reviewed access mechanism; public filesystem paths and unbounded permanent bearer URLs are not the default.

title: Teluni Deployment and Migration Planning
heading: Backup and restore requirements
text:
Backup and restore requirements
Backups must cover PostgreSQL, media, future provider identity state and the non-secret configuration/release metadata needed to reconstruct operation. Review future session persistence separately: restoring old sessions must never resurrect revoked access; session invalidation/reauthentication may be necessary. Provider signing material and authentication recovery require a protected, separately controlled recovery path, not plaintext configuration exports. Protect and recover secrets through a separate controlled process. A database-only backup is insufficient if it points to unavailable media.
Choose a consistency method for the database-plus-files set, backup schedule, off-host destination, encryption/key recovery, retention, capacity and success/failure reporting. A second directory on the same disk does not cover loss of the host. Local budget constraints do not eliminate the need to resolve off-host recovery before accepting private customer data.
Rehearse restore into an isolated environment: verify migration/application compatibility, ownership/permissions, manifest-to-file integrity, representative playback and tenant access, then reconcile revoked identities and deletion/retention obligations. Record achieved recovery point/time and compare them with owner-approved RPO/RTO. Preserve audit/release history; do not restore stale authorization silently.

title: Teluni Deployment and Migration Planning
heading: Future host or storage migration
text:
Future host or storage migration
**Proposed sequence**, to turn into tested runbooks once topology and credentials exist:
Inventory supported player versions, configurable API/media addresses, tenant data, assets, release versions and secret destinations. Prepare DNS/certificate ownership and compatible software at the destination.
Rehearse backup restore and file verification without customer writes. Determine whether logical object IDs remain stable and how private media authorization is preserved.
Plan a bounded write cutover or verified incremental reconciliation to avoid divergent metadata and media. Preserve audit and device identities without exposing their credentials.
Update endpoints through the approved mechanism with certificate validation and rollback capability. Keep the old address/redirect or compatibility path only for an explicitly defined overlap, accounting for long-offline players. Never accept arbitrary redirected credential recipients.
Verify representative players reconnect, reconcile desired/active versions, and continue offline playback. Check uploads, access denial, publication, backups and monitoring on the new host.
Close the rollback window deliberately, reconcile retained data/deletions and retire old storage/credentials safely. The endpoint overlap and maximum supported offline interval must be compatible; unresolved unreachable devices require a support plan.
Triggers for migration include measured cost/availability/support risk, storage or uplink saturation, growth, or earned revenue supporting operations. Cloud procurement and live migration are outside this documentation task.

title: Teluni Offline Playback and Synchronization
heading: Teluni Offline Playback and Synchronization
text:
Teluni Offline Playback and Synchronization
[Requirements](mvp.md) · [Release policies](release-policies.md) · [Acceptance targets](release-targets.md) · [ADR-0019 decision](../adr/0019-propose-immutable-publications-and-atomic-player-activation.md)

title: Teluni Offline Playback and Synchronization
heading: Required guarantees and implementation boundary
text:
Required guarantees and implementation boundary
**Decided requirements:** local media and catalog rendering through the bounded offline envelope, integrity validation, complete-generation activation and last-valid recovery. Normal video playback does not stream repeatedly from the backend. Freeform composition, independently scheduled areas with optional page coordination, multiple videos/audio and typed custom catalogs must meet the same obligations.
PH-09 has selected product behavior and numeric qualification targets. Protocol/schema serialization, integrity metadata/algorithms, local transactions/storage, processing/rendering libraries, transport and credential/trusted-time mechanisms remain engineering review under D-03/D-04/D-05/D-07/D-11. [ADR-0023](../adr/0023-propose-versioned-catalog-and-composition-publications.md) establishes the accepted versioned catalog/composition boundary; neither ADR is an implemented protocol or evidence of durability.

title: Teluni Offline Playback and Synchronization
heading: Publication lifecycle
text:
Publication lifecycle
An authorized publisher deliberately publishes ordinary draft state. A designated price save instead automatically records publication intent for affected published bindings under the release policies; it does not release unrelated layout/schema/record drafts.
Validate actor/target tenant and branch scope, schema/record/field bindings, compatible rendering/media profiles, scheduling, effective prices and durable media. Build an immutable complete snapshot with the rules/data needed for offline interpretation. Desired availability must not precede durable assets and metadata.
Record the desired generation and required work durably. A database update and media filesystem writes are not one transaction. Stage/verify objects, then commit references/intent with recoverable cleanup and reconciliation. Follow delivery policy; an in-memory after-commit callback alone cannot guarantee price/publication fan-out.
The independently authenticated device reconciles its authorized desired generation and local active/staged state. It receives only compatible tenant-scoped rules, schema/record snapshots and media descriptors. A content path is not immutable identity when its bytes can change.
Preflight space for staged plus protected active/recovery resources and the target reserve, counting shared files once. Download absent/changed assets with bounded timeouts/retries. Interrupted files cannot masquerade as complete; refreshing download authorization cannot make private media public.
Verify expected length/integrity, references, schema interpretation and renderer/media capability before accepting resources. A checksum detects corruption but does not authenticate an untrusted manifest by itself. Preserve valid active output on invalid or incomplete staging.
Prepare the complete supported local generation, then durably activate it. Keep publication selection distinct from the schedule that chooses its eligible output. Atomic-generation recovery and safe resource release need actual power-cut tests; do not overwrite active files progressively.
Report desired, received/staged and reported-active facts separately. Repeated/lost acknowledgements must reconcile; server acceptance is not proof of TV activation. The panel represents active A plus failed staging B without calling every sync failure a playback outage.
Retain the previous valid generation and protected staging resources under retention/reference rules. Restore only if still authorized, compatible and commercially valid. Do not resurrect expired promotions, deleted ownership or revoked credentials.
Confirmed assignment/source changes use the latest published programming without another content publish action. An explicitly confirmed destination with no first publication produces authorized neutral no-programming output after the assignment is applied. This deliberate empty source differs from failed/corrupt synchronization, which preserves valid state. An unreachable player cannot apply an unseen assignment or erasure.
Candidate logical states such as unpaired, no-content, staging, active, degraded and pending-clear describe concurrent facts, not committed enum/API names. Their exact schema must preserve the distinctions above.

title: Teluni Offline Playback and Synchronization
heading: Consistency and concurrency
text:
Consistency and concurrency
Publication/price-save/download/acknowledgement operations need explicit idempotency, stale-write detection, retry ownership, bounded attempts and observable failure/reconciliation. Do not treat a mutation timeout as certain failure or retry an unprotected side effect.
Order desired state using authoritative generation/revision information, not device wall-clock order. Old acknowledgements and stale processing cannot roll a target back to an earlier price or assignment.
Under the owner's delegation, prefer the latest authorized compatible desired snapshot and permit coalescing superseded pending delivery work. Keep attributable publication/price history and every still-valid schedule in the latest snapshot; coalescing delivery is not deleting audit events or omitting future programmed transitions.
Use published dependency revisions for automatic price publication. Concurrent schema/layout drafts remain separate. Expose saved/queued/publication-failed states, reconcile incomplete fan-out and never claim successful device distribution from the catalog transaction alone.
Typed schema evolution/import and reference validation are part of publication validity. A record/field reference cannot bypass tenant/branch authorization or select another tenant through a custom value.
Retry elapsed time is separate from business scheduling. Respect application shutdown and bounded work claims; a crashed worker must not lose required intent or leave inaccessible staging permanently.

title: Teluni Offline Playback and Synchronization
heading: Time and regional scheduling
text:
Time and regional scheduling
[Release policies](release-policies.md#time-and-scheduling) own the exact calendar/DST/overnight/date-clipping and conflict rules. Backend preview and player must share fixtures for them, regional overrides/page coordination, promotional price validity, pagination and no-match output. Store/compare instants while retaining the geographic zone needed for recurring local time; never inherit the backend host timezone.
An active regional schedule controls its area's output even while the underlying page changes. On ending, return to the applicable current-page/default/neutral state without restarting independent areas. Coordinated page-controlled participants use a common transition point; ordinary short-video completion holds the last frame while the page continues. Schedule boundaries interrupt affected output and override fades/page/item completion without extending expired content.
A regional rendering failure inside an active valid generation may use its still-valid local contingency or neutral area and report degradation while other areas continue. This runtime isolation does not permit activation of a publication with missing/corrupt required resources. A recovered coordinated area rejoins the current valid page/schedule state; it does not replay expired content or reset every area.

title: Teluni Offline Playback and Synchronization
heading: Authorization, clock and recovery boundaries
text:
Authorization, clock and recovery boundaries
The [target specification](release-targets.md#reliability-and-synchronization-targets) defines offline authorization and trusted-clock limits. Authorization expiry gives neutral output and requires reconnection; a restored cache cannot extend it. Server revocation rejects new protected operations while a disconnected cache may persist until local authorization expires. Erasure is pending until actually observed, and another tenant cannot pair before verified cleanup/reset.
Detectable clock jumps or insufficient trusted-time confidence suspend time-dependent schedules/prices. Do not claim an incorrect wall clock can always be detected without a reference. If remaining authorization validity cannot be established safely, protected playback must also stop; a local setup/neutral view does not disclose private tenant data. Reboot/offline time estimation and established credential/cryptographic components require threat-model review and qualified tests before delivery.
Initial pairing/synchronization requires backend access. With no valid installed program show safe local setup/no-content output. A publication's optional default or neutral fallback is evaluated locally within authorization and content-validity rules, not permission to replay stale commercial data indefinitely.

title: Teluni Offline Playback and Synchronization
heading: Failure and recovery acceptance
text:
Failure and recovery acceptance
Condition
Required observable outcome / evidence
Server/network outage after sync
Local media/catalog/region scheduling continues within AT-10/AT-15/AT-16; verify expected neutral state at expiry/uncertain time
Interrupted download or expired access
Safe bounded retry/resume only when verified; active generation continues; no partial asset activation
Invalid schema, binding, manifest, media or incompatible profile
Reject staging with bounded actionable diagnostics; keep active valid output; no infinite hot retry or cross-tenant reference
Insufficient storage/memory
Respect AT-05, refuse unsafe preparation and preserve active/recovery assets; do not remove functions silently
Power/process failure at prepare/switch
Recover a complete eligible generation and reconcile partial/orphan staging; qualify AT-06–AT-10 on representative devices
Duplicate/reordered/concurrent price/publication work
Reconcile idempotently; exclude unrelated drafts, stale-price rollback and mixed generations
Regional runtime failure or no-match
Isolate the affected output under policy, retain other geometry/output and report actual degradation
Date/DST/clock/promotion boundary
Preview/player fixture agreement and AT-13/AT-16; never revive expired output through fallback or rollback
Revoked/unlinked/unreachable device
Reject future protected access; enforce local authorization deadline; distinguish pending/confirmed erasure and require cleanup before reassignment
Incompatible generation or failed player update
Follow AT-26 support window; preserve allowed playback, report incompatibility, use qualified update/rollback recovery
Host move or database/media restore
Reconcile device intent, ownership/revocation and publication resources in an isolated rehearsal; never leak credentials or point devices at an untested recovery endpoint
Every interruption boundary needs automated contract/security fixtures and physical hardware/network/power evidence, not only happy-path mocks. All future product target measurements remain pending. PH-08/PJ-12/PJ-14 own device qualification; PH-10/PJ-13 own host/restore/migration readiness.

heading: Purpose and positioning
text:
Purpose and positioning
**Decided:** Teluni is a multi-tenant digital signage SaaS for centralized management of visual content on televisions, monitors, and other display devices. It should combine simple operation, reliable local playback, freeform simultaneous presentation and configurable data-driven content. Brazil is the initial market, with international commercialization anticipated. The owner selected initial capabilities for product quality rather than limiting them solely by the MVP label.

Origin and pilot

The owner selected Apache-2.0 for Teluni source and documentation; [ADR-0022](../adr/0022-license-teluni-under-apache-2-0.md) records that decision and [PH-06](human-actions.md#ph-06) records its verification. title: Teluni Product Vision
heading: Actors and core journeys
text:
Actors and core journeys
The [security model](security-and-i18n.md#actors-and-authorization) routes to the selected human access policies and their pending technical enforcement. The product journeys are:
A verified eligible registrant creates a new company through public automatic activation and becomes its responsible administrator, subject to commercial/privacy/abuse readiness. The platform retains a controlled assisted-enrollment path without claiming existing companies by name or domain.
A company administrator creates branches and delegates permitted operations to members.
An authorized operator pairs a display using a temporary code shown by the player and assigns it to the correct branch.
An authorized publisher uploads media, configures typed catalogs/fields/records (for example products or a weekly agenda), composes regional content/schedules, previews and publishes.
Authorized price saves automatically publish affected already-published data bindings, without releasing unrelated drafts or recreating artwork. Other draft edits retain explicit publication.
The player stages complete consistent versions and continues local media/catalog rendering through the selected offline/clock envelope, with independent areas or optional coordinated pages.
A scoped operator sees last contact, synchronization progress and actionable failures without unrestricted remote access. Actual player observation is distinct from server intent.
Acceptance of these journeys is specified in [release requirements](mvp.md). The owner selected [human identity/access policies](identity-and-access.md), including public signup with automatic company activation, Google-only external login, multi-company memberships, a responsible administrator and customizable scoped profiles. The owner accepted the architecture ADRs and completed PH-11 decision selection; actual Keycloak/session qualification and external readiness remain pending; no signup/session flow is implemented.

**Decided:** recurring SaaS is the intended business model. **Proposed:** charge primarily by number of screens, potentially with a company minimum and feature-based plans. Decision status and ownership
**Decided on 2026-10-18:** these product policies consolidate the owner's questionnaire and the remaining choices explicitly delegated to engineering. They extend the earlier company-to-screen requirements to freeform composition and configurable catalogs. Product capability and quality take priority over reducing scope solely for an MVP label. [Acceptance targets](release-targets.md) own numeric limits and qualification goals; [playback/sync](playback-and-sync.md) owns the proposed delivery lifecycle; [architecture](architecture.md#pending-decisions) and ADRs own remaining technical choices. PH-08/PH-10/PH-11/PH-13 and PJ-07 retain their separate hardware, operations, identity, privacy and architecture reviews.

title: Teluni Release Policies
heading: Assignment and publication
text:
Assignment and publication
Support individual-device assignment and persistent company-owned groups. A device belongs to zero or one programming group; a group may span authorized branches of the same company. Check all target references and permissions on the server.
A grouped device follows its group unless an authorized user explicitly selects individual programming. That choice replaces the complete group programming, retains membership and is visibly identified in the panel. Returning to the group is explicit; a membership edit does not silently remove the exception.
Confirming an assignment/source change requests the destination's latest published programming without another publish action. An intentionally unpublished destination is permitted after a clear pre-confirmation indication: after applying the authorized change, the player shows local neutral output until its first valid publication. A failed or unseen synchronization instead preserves valid state.
Ordinary layout, schema, record, playlist and schedule edits are drafts until deliberately published. An exception applies to an authorized **price save**: it automatically records publication intent for affected published bindings and produces a new validated version. A price save never mutates a snapshot in place or publishes unrelated drafts. This exception concerns designated monetary price semantics, not every numeric/custom field.
[PH-11 identity/access policies](identity-and-access.md#publication-impact-and-delayed-work) require whole-mutation rejection when any affected target is unauthorized, without partial distribution or automatic approval fallback. Optional company approval rules distinguish a proposal from the effective price save: only an authorized independent approval commits the effective price and initiates automatic publication. No proposal is reported as an already-applied price.
Distinguish saved, queued, failed, published, downloaded and active states. If automatic price publication fails, show the pending/failure state and retry/reconcile durably; do not report that disconnected TVs have changed. Duplicate saves/retries and concurrent edits must not replay an obsolete price over a newer one. Invalid input is rejected before accepting a price change.
A publication contains consistent layout/schema/record/price/media versions. Activation requires its complete supported resource set; failure preserves the last valid generation. Rollback still applies current authorization and content-validity rules and cannot resurrect an expired promotion.
